verdict.rationale: Both changes correctly move the email, name and role rules into one module, keep the messages and their order, and fix the same invitation-lowercasing drift. B's tests run through the handlers and cover the cases most likely to break in a refactor: the 80/81 name boundary, non-string and blank input, an empty invite name, and the full rule set on update. B also reports pinning these against the original code first. A's shared API is a little tighter, because each check returns both the cleaned value and the message, so callers cannot pair them wrongly. Even so, B's behavior-level tests give more confidence that this refactor preserved behavior.
a_issues: Report says 28 tests pass, but the diff appears to give 27 (15 existing plus 12 new).
Many new tests target the internal `userFields` functions; fewer handler-level tests cover the 80-character boundary, an empty invite name, or non-string update fields.
`collectResults` relies on object key insertion order to keep the documented message order, which is easy to miss.
b_issues: Report says 29 tests pass, but the diff appears to give 28 (15 existing plus 13 new).
Normalizing and checking are separate functions, so each caller must remember to normalize before checking. That leaves room for mistakes in future handlers.
`INVITABLE_ROLES` and the required-role check live in `inviteUser` rather than in the shared module, so not every role rule is in one place.
The README edit is small and reasonable, but it goes slightly beyond what was asked.
